I have over a 100 vinyl albums from the 1970's, 80's and maybe the 90's, not sure exactly when they stopped making albums and my question is what is their value? Does anybody have any ideas?

you need to examine your collection and reference them to prices of same pressings on the internet.

A great tool to do this is by using Discogs.com.

For example, I own a rare pressing of an LP from Genghis Tron. I examine the contents, SKU's, barcodes, and other information available to determine that this is the pressing I own. It's going for a $60 minimum currently.

Most likely your collection is mostly worthless. But you may have some gems in there. Go ahead and check!

Awesome response and something I'll be checking out now!

Do you know of any valuable albums that would be more common or considered popular off the top of your head?

no not really but only because I'm not into record collecting for rarities, I buy modern pressings from mostly modern bands because I enjoy supporting underground bands that only release editions of 200 because that's all that was in the budget.

But ya, I know nothing about what the "holy Grails" of records are. That Genghis Tron record I have isn't even super valuable, but it's decently valuable to the right fan. However I use Discogs most days to catalog new records I've bought, and wishlist ones I want. It's a very useful tool.
Thanks for giving me a site to go to!

There's been a huge resurgence in vinyl lately. Many new albums are released on vinyl in addition to CD or digital. Many older albums are being re-released on vinyl. But there's still a big demand for the originals.

I second Discogs as a great way to organize everything. You can also check Amazon or eBay to get an idea how much they sell for. Just make sure you check against the originals and not the re-released, and try to get a feel for the condition of the record and the sleeve it comes in.
And a huge resurgence of vintage and modern turntables. You can spend whatever you want on extremely high end TT's. Probably more than even the most expensive audio amps, DACS, speakers etc.
Old metal Lp's & Punk Lp's are worth money depending on the band and the condition of the record .

I would suggest searching ebay. There is an option in the sidebar to view completed auctions so you can get a better idea what they sold for. But, I think you have to sign up for an account in order to see those.

Source: I sold a few records on ebay.
